target_customer: Auto parts retailers and ecommerce sellers with inaccurate supplier product data
problem: Supplier part data is inconsistent and incomplete; retailers need titles, descriptions and specs per marketplace guidelines.
business_model: B2B SaaS for catalog enhancement (pricing not found)
product_category: AI product-data enrichment for automotive aftermarket

founders.name: Christina Seong
founders.background_notes: No prior automotive experience per a 2024 profile (Pulse 2.0).

technical_complexity.rationale: Scraping part listings and fine-tuning an LLM with retrieval to generate fitment-aware descriptions from a part number, at a time when LLMs were just becoming usable.

defensibility.rationale: Accumulated parts records database and marketplace guideline ingestion help, but the approach is replicable.

incumbents: Catalog data vendors such as SEMA Data Co-op and DCi
takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent action found; a 2024 profile says rivals mostly use rule-based enhancement.

market_need_then: Auto parts ecommerce growth and industry-standard data (ACES/PIES) that suppliers adopt voluntarily leave gaps; the founder describes a 500B+ dollar market.

brand_strength.rationale: Only a 2024 profile and the YC pages exist; nothing on brand perception.

outcome_analysis: Versable is a three-person company serving auto parts retailers with LLM-generated product data, and went through a private beta before a public launch around July 2024. Reported funding is small and mostly from YC and angels. There is no evidence of large traction or an exit, so it is a slow-growing niche startup whose outcome is unresolved.
notes: Total raised 2.6M (investors YC, Bling Capital, Soma Capital) appears in a single 2024 founder profile with no dates; aggregators say 2.6-3.1M. Not recorded as a round.
